sections.title: Project Overview
blocks: **Expertise:** Website Strategy, Visual Design, Content Strategy, International Marketing, Project Management
The redesigned English website has officially launched, providing information for international travelers and supporting their direct-booking journey and the hotel's international marketing.
**Live Website:** https://www.nobogura.co.jp/en/

sections.title: The Challenge
blocks: As the hotel increased its focus on FIT rather than group and package tours, the English website needed to help international guests research, compare and book with confidence.
@challenge-illustration

What feels obvious to Japanese guests may be unfamiliar to international travelers. Translation alone cannot explain practical details such as transport, room types and onsen etiquette in the order they need them.

Drawing on my experience planning independent trips, I recognized the importance of presenting the hotel's traditional onsen identity and unique experiences in a way international travelers could easily understand.

sections.title: Strategic Approach
blocks: Rather than treating the project as a translation exercise or visual refresh, I approached the website as a customer-centric marketing platform.
@strategy-framework
- **Customer-Centric Content:** Address international travelers' practical needs.
- **Information Architecture:** Make information easy to locate, understand and compare.
- **Visual Communication:** Use imagery and layout to convey the guest experience.
- **Destination Marketing:** Connect the hotel with Noboribetsu and nearby experiences.
- **Direct Booking Support:** Guide visitors from research to the hotel's booking system.

sections.title: My Role & Delivery
blocks: ### My Role — Overseas Marketing Manager
I led the marketing direction, content strategy, visual design and agency coordination for the project.

I personally designed the layouts, typography, font sizes, image selection and information hierarchy, balancing visual consistency with useful information. The goal was a website that answered travelers' questions, not just made a strong visual impression.
- Defined marketing objectives and analyzed international traveler needs.
- Developed content strategy and information architecture.
- Prepared content, images and implementation requirements.
- Coordinated with the external development agency.
- Reviewed content, design consistency and implementation quality.
### External Agency
The external agency handled technical development, programming and implementation of the design, including revisions based on feedback.

sections.title: Introduction
blocks: With a background in Human Resources and Learning & Development, combined with hands-on experience in international marketing within Japan's hospitality industry, my work brings together a traveler's perspective, creativity and management experience.

sections.title: Think Like a Traveler
blocks: Travel has always been a source of inspiration. Planning independent trips across Kanto, Kansai and Hokkaido has offered opportunities to explore nature, onsen, cuisine, art, cultural festivals and entertainment.

Beyond the experiences themselves, observing how businesses present their products, communicate information and shape customer experiences offers valuable insights into marketing from an international traveler's perspective.

sections.title: Continuous Learning
blocks: I began learning Japanese at 32. Nearly two and a half years later, I have passed JLPT N3 and am now studying toward N2. Learning a new language as an adult has taught me the value of persistence, patience and starting from scratch. I bring that same commitment to learning and improving my skills to my work.

sections.title: Management & Leadership
blocks: Nine years of experience in Human Resources and Learning & Development within international hotels and Japanese companies have provided a foundation in management, team development, resource planning and coordination.
This experience also informs my approach to marketing projects, connecting creative ideas with business objectives through planning, decision-making and execution.

sections.title: Project Background
blocks: In addition to promoting the products and services of Noboribetsu Grand Hotel, I focus on leveraging local tourism resources to enhance the appeal of the destination and expand the hotel's brand awareness in international markets.

sections.title: Market & Audience Insights
blocks: ### B2C — International FIT
From a FIT perspective, I recognize that international visitors may struggle to find information about lesser-known local experiences.
Providing this information helps guests plan their own trips while giving them additional reasons to choose the hotel for their stay.
### B2B — International Travel Trade

To expand brand awareness in English-speaking markets, I approach international travel companies by highlighting the commercial value of the destination, opportunities to incorporate local experiences into travel itineraries, and the potential for accommodation partnerships.

sections.title: Strategic Approach
blocks: - **Destination Research:** Research tourism resources, local experiences and seasonal activities.
- **Audience-Specific Marketing:** Develop marketing messages and materials tailored to B2C and B2B audiences.
- **Hotel Positioning:** Position the hotel as a convenient base for travelers and a potential accommodation partner for travel companies.
